comments.body:
AC1 — the 449f hypothesis is **REFUTED**, decisively, with runtime evidence from the very run it was raised against.

## Experiment 1 — the mechanism itself (local, git 2.55.0)

Built a bare origin with `main` + `tickets`, then a workspace whose `remote.origin.fetch`
was set explicitly, emulating reconcile-bridge.yml:115 (explicit refspec creates
`origin/tickets`), then let a third party advance the true remote branch, then ran the
site under test — a bare `git fetch origin tickets`:

    configured +refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main   (narrow)
      origin/tickets before : 3c477492
      true remote tickets   : 2322aded
      FETCH_HEAD after      : 2322aded
      origin/tickets after  : 3c477492   -> STALE

    configured +refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*         (wildcard)
      origin/tickets before : 3c477492
      true remote tickets   : 2322aded
      origin/tickets after  : 2322aded   -> ADVANCED

So the stale-ref mechanism is real — but it is conditional on a NARROW configured refspec.

## Experiment 2 — is that precondition true in CI? NO.

`actions/checkout` builds its workspace with `git remote add origin <url>`, and
`git remote add` installs the DEFAULT WILDCARD refspec (verified directly:
`git init && git remote add origin <url>` -> `remote.origin.fetch = +refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*`).
The real runner log for run **30585738860** — one of the four cited mode-2 push-rejection
failures — confirms it: `git remote add origin https://github.com/navapbc/rebar` followed by
`git -c protocol.version=2 fetch ... origin +refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/* +refs/tags/*:refs/tags/*`,
with no `git config remote.origin.fetch` narrowing anywhere in the job.

## Experiment 3 — direct observation of the ref in the failing run

The same run log shows the bare fetch UPDATING the remote-tracking ref on every single
retry:

    60ccc6506..4d37b6925  tickets -> origin/tickets
    4d37b6925..dd70be0d7  tickets -> origin/tickets
    dd70be0d7..a46013f4c  tickets -> origin/tickets
    a46013f4c..f3a1fe61f  tickets -> origin/tickets

Four distinct advances, each followed by a "Merge made by the 'ort' strategy" integrating
new event files. That is the exact opposite of the predicted stale-ref signature, which
requires the ref to stay pinned. 449f mode 2 was a genuine push race — as 449f already
concluded and fixed under 4c4f (backoff removal) — not a stale merge target.

**Conclusion: the workflow bare-fetch sites were NOT causing 449f, and are not causing any
observed failure.** No link to 449f is being made; the hypothesis is dead. The workflow
change in this ticket is therefore hardening/consistency, not a defect fix: it removes a
dependency on a third-party action's internal choice of `git remote add`, and it is a
behavioural no-op today.

## What IS a live defect: push.py:182

Drove the real `push.push_tickets_branch` under a narrow refspec with a competing writer
on origin/tickets. Only the configured refspec differs between the two runs:

    narrow   -> "tickets branch push failed (merge conflict, attempt 1/2/3)"
                "tickets branch push failed after 3 retries"
                PUSH CONVERGED: False | competing events absorbed: False
    wildcard -> PUSH CONVERGED: True  | competing events absorbed: True

The bare fetch leaves `origin/tickets` absent, `git merge origin/tickets` fails, the loop
misreports it as a merge conflict, and every retry re-pushes the same rejected history.
This reaches ordinary users: a single-branch/`--depth` clone is exactly the configuration
bug 5546 proved occurs for this repo/branch/remote triple.

## Scope note

`push.py`'s merge carries NO `--allow-unrelated-histories` (verified), so reaching the
merge cannot union unrelated histories. 5546's `_carries_ticket_events` merge-safety
predicate has no analogue here and was deliberately NOT replicated — this change is a
refspec change and nothing else.

## Summary

Sibling sweep of bug 5546 (rebar-debug Step 7). 5546's root cause is a repeatable
pattern, not a one-off: **a bare `git fetch <remote> <branch>` whose result is then
consumed as `<remote>/<branch>`.** A bare fetch always writes FETCH_HEAD but only
*opportunistically* writes `refs/remotes/<remote>/<branch>` — and only when the remote's
CONFIGURED refspec covers that branch. Under a narrow refspec
(`+refs/heads/main:refs/remotes/origin/main`, which is what `git clone --single-branch`
AND `actions/checkout` produce by default) the ref is never written, or — worse, when it
already exists — never UPDATED, so the consumer silently reads a missing or STALE ref.

5546 fixed the `sync.py` instance. Two live instances remain; both were confirmed
semantically (read in context), not by string match.

## Sibling 1 — `src/rebar/_store/push.py:182`

```python
_git(base_path, "fetch", remote, branch)          # :182  bare fetch
...
merge = _git(base_path, "merge", remote_ref, ...) # :202  consumes f"{remote}/{branch}"
```

This is the non-fast-forward retry loop. Under a narrow refspec the merge target is
missing or stale, so the merge cannot absorb what actually rejected the push and **every
retry re-pushes the same rejected history until the budget is exhausted.**

## Sibling 2 — `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:286,309` (and the canary at :424,:436)

```sh
git fetch origin tickets || true                      # :286
ahead=$(git rev-list --count origin/tickets..HEAD ...) # :287  consumes origin/tickets
...
git fetch origin tickets 2>&1 || ...                  # :309  inside the retry loop
```

Note the SAME workflow already uses the correct explicit form at line 115
(`git fetch origin '+tickets:refs/remotes/origin/tickets'`), as does
`verify-identity.yml:55` — so these sites are internally inconsistent, which is good
evidence they are an oversight rather than a deliberate choice.

**This is a strong candidate root cause for bug 449f-f9bf-be90-47fe** (and for the
Reconcile Bridge push-rejection evidence recorded in 5546's own comment thread: 4 runs on
2026-07-30 exhausting a 5-retry budget with `! [rejected] HEAD -> tickets (fetch first)`).
Because line 115 creates `refs/remotes/origin/tickets` earlier in the job, the later bare
fetches at :286/:309 leave it STALE rather than absent — so `rev-list origin/tickets..HEAD`
and the reconcile merge both operate on a snapshot that never advances, and the retry loop
provably cannot converge no matter how large the budget. That mechanism has NOT yet been
experimentally confirmed against a real runner; it is a cited hypothesis, and confirming or
rejecting it is the first task here.

## Deliberately NOT siblings (checked and cleared)

- `src/rebar/opcert_service/workspace.py:70,87` — bare fetch, then consumes
  `review/<branch>` / `tickets/<branch>`. Same shape, but the workspace is built by
  `git init` + `git remote add`, which installs the DEFAULT WILDCARD refspec, so the
  branch is always covered. Not reachable.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/_ref_lock.py:347`, `review_bot/gerrit_client.py:335`,
  `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:115`, `reconcile-bridge-canary.yml:86`,
  `verify-identity.yml:55` — already use an explicit refspec. Correct as written.
- `src/rebar/_commands/init.py:375` — a genuine instance, but bug 01e8-302b-ab8f-4220
  already owns and fixes it. Excluded to avoid a conflicting edit.

## Why filed rather than folded into 5546

5546's authorized surface was `src/rebar/_store/sync.py` + its tests. `push.py` and the
CI workflows are separate blast radii — the workflow change in particular needs a real
runner to verify — so they get their own reviewable change rather than riding along.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The 449f hypothesis above is experimentally confirmed or rejected against a real
      narrow-refspec checkout; if confirmed, 449f is linked to this ticket.
- [ ] `push.py`'s retry-loop fetch uses an explicit refspec, with a test proving the
      non-fast-forward retry loop converges under a narrow clone refspec (it currently
      cannot).
- [ ] The reconcile-bridge workflows' bare `git fetch origin tickets` sites use the
      explicit refspec already used at line 115 of the same file.
- [ ] A guard (lint rule, test, or reviewer-facing note) prevents the bare-fetch form
      from being reintroduced.
